_doc: WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The owner's phone is set to Spanish and reads these apps in Spanish. Nothing in this repository noticed when a string landed in values/strings.xml without a translation: Android lint's MissingTranslation is the rule that would catch it, but no workflow in .github/workflows/ ever invokes a `lint` task at all (CI runs `assembleRelease` and nothing else), and the three modules that DO configure the rule have each turned it off — cloud-vault disables it in three build.gradle.kts lint blocks, cloud-matrix sets it to `ignore` in tools/lint/lint.xml, cloud-dialer downgrades it to `warning`. So the rule was reported nowhere and enforced nowhere, and cloud-mail accumulated 89 English strings inside a Spanish app while cloud-superapp, cloud-ide and libs:mail never got a translated locale at all. cloud-android-i18n-guard.py reads this file and fails the build instead.

locale._doc: WHY `es` AND NOT `es-rES`. The owner's device asks for Spanish (Spain) — recent work set the keyboard defaults to Espanol (Espana). Android resolves a request for es-ES by trying values-es-rES first and then falling back to the language-only values-es, so BOTH directories reach this device; values-es additionally reaches es-MX, es-AR and every other Spanish region, and values-es-rES reaches none of them. The narrower directory buys nothing here and costs every other Spanish variant. It is also what the repository already does and already says: ac_cloud-mail ships values-es and the owner reads that app in Spanish today, which is direct proof the device consults it, and the comment above status_light_on in aa_cloud-superapp/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml instructs whoever adds the first locale to add `values-es`.

modules._doc: Every module in the repository that owns a src/main/res/values/strings.xml must appear here, or the guard fails. That is deliberate and it is the answer to 'what happens to the NEXT app the owner builds': a new module with a new strings.xml is not silently exempt, it stops CI until somebody states in this file whether its interface has to be readable in Spanish. `require` lists locale qualifiers that must cover every translatable key. `exempt` is a sentence saying why not, and is read by a human in review.
